title: Re-mount a suction grab bar pressed on over the grout line: hold it, release both cups, move it onto tile, relock
instruction: Fix the suction grab bar on the tiled panel so that it holds.
context: Suction grab bars give a hand-hold for balance at the bath, basin or WC. Their makers say they hold on smooth, airtight surfaces only, with both cups wholly on tile at least 1/2 inch from all grout lines or joints, and to check before each use that both indicators show green: a cup over the grout lets air in and the bar comes off when it is leaned on. Here someone has pressed the bar on with its right cup across the grout line; that cup's indicator shows red, the left one green. The bar must be released and set again with both cups on tile. Releasing a cup lets the bar drop, and flipping a lever pushes on the bar: one hand holds the bar flat against the tiles while the other works the levers. Each lever sits at its cup's outer end: pulled out, it releases the cup; pushed home along the housing's end while the cup is pressed to the wall, it locks it.
setup: Station bench; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x towards the panel, y left. Both arms at the ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout; nothing varies by seed. Panel (a test fixture): two white glossy glazed wall tiles 25 x 40 x 0.8 cm side by side on an 18 mm multiplex board 52 x 40 cm with a 3 mm open joint (tile spacers), stood upright on two steel angle brackets, tile face at x = 34, joint upright at y = 0, bottom on the bench. Bar: Wenko Wandgriff Secura, 29 cm, white, maker's no. 7820100 (on sale as Wenko Wannengriff Secura 290 mm, OBI 9808973; US: Drive Medical suction cup grab bar RTL13083, 12 in), two 9.5 cm cups, each locked by a flip lever at its housing's outer end, a red/green indicator tab on top; level on the panel, its middle 7 cm over the bench and 6 cm left of the joint (y = +6): the right cup across the joint, its lever locked and its tab red; the left cup wholly on the left tile, its lever locked and its tab green. The start is checked against tape marks and a photo from the top camera.
scoring: Read when the trial ends; it ends early once the full score has held 2 s. 0 for the whole trial if the bar touches the bench at any moment. Otherwise, with both grippers 3 cm or more from the bar and the bar and its levers at rest (the cups count as part of the bar): 1.0 both cups wholly on tile, their rims at least 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) from the joint and 5 mm from the tiles' outer edges, both levers locked and sealed (green), the bar within 10 degrees of level; 0.5 both cups clear, one sealed; 0 otherwise. A lever locked over a cup across the joint or nearer it than 1/2 inch, or not pressed flat onto the tile so its tab shows green, seals nothing. On the bench: a ruler from each rim to the joint and the tiles' edges, the red and green tabs, a level app on the grip; the bench touch is read from the trial video.
reset_notes: Release both levers, take the bar off and press it on again with its middle on the tape marks (7 cm over the bench, 6 cm left of the joint), then lock both levers: the right tab shows red. Under a minute; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at true size. A cup holds once its lever passes centre with the cup pressed on with 12 N or more (estimate) and its rim on one tile 1/2 inch or more from the joint (the makers' rule); otherwise it holds nothing. The 3 mm open joint stands for grout: both let air in under a rim. The levers sit at the housings' outer ends and the indicator tabs on top, as on the named bars. Rubber flex, air leakage and the tile's grip on a loaded cup are not modelled.
